title: How Feeding Babies Works: The Bottle
summary: Part two of the How Feeding Babies Works series, focused on bottle feeding. The hosts cover mastitis and breast implants as reasons some women don't breastfeed, the history of wet nurses and Soranus of Ephesus's consistency test, the rise of infant formula (Justus von Liebig's formula, Gail Borden's condensed milk, evaporated milk, the 1974 Nestlé scandal and the 1980 FDA oversight), milk banks and informal milk sharing, breast pumps, nipple preference, formula ingredients and water safety, bottle warming, bottle materials and BPA, safe bottle-feeding positions, burping, feeding schedules, and the role of dads. The episode ends with a listener suggestion about explorer John Evans and the book American Interior.

segments.title: SF Sketch Fest promo and intro
segments.summary: Hosts promote their San Francisco SF Sketch Fest show, then open the episode as part two of How Feeding Babies Works.

segments.title: Mastitis and breast implants as barriers to breastfeeding
segments.summary: The hosts describe mastitis, a painful breast inflammation that can lead mothers to stop breastfeeding, and explain how breast implant incisions, nerve damage, and implant placement affect the ability to breastfeed.

segments.title: Wet nurses and breastfeeding history
segments.summary: The hosts discuss reasons women choose not to breastfeed, then cover the history of wet nurses, who were mainly used by wealthier families, and shifting views on breastfeeding versus formula over time.

segments.title: Soranus's breast milk consistency test
segments.summary: Soranus of Ephesus wrote an early obstetrics and pediatrics treatise that included a fingernail test for breast milk consistency, used for about fifteen hundred years. Animal milk use is also mentioned.

segments.title: Invention of infant formula and early condensed milk
segments.summary: Early formula history: the feeding bottle arrived in France, Liebig developed a powdered formula in 1865, early deaths from unsterilized feeding led to germ theory and sterilization, and Gail Borden's condensed milk and Marling's evaporated milk were used as infant food.

segments.title: Formula becomes medicalized and the Nestlé scandal
segments.summary: Formula gained a medical image in the 1930s to 1950s, with manufacturers advertising only to doctors. The 1974 Nestlé marketing scandal in developing countries, involving contaminated water, eroded trust. The FDA was tasked with formula oversight in 1980, and formula ads went to the public in the late 1980s.

segments.title: Milk banks and informal milk sharing
segments.summary: Milk banks sell screened donor breast milk for around five dollars an ounce with a prescription, with some insurers covering it. Informal options such as Only the Breast, MilkShare, and cross nursing among friends carry the risk of unscreened milk.

segments.title: Breast pump history and nipple preference
segments.summary: The breast pump dates to the nineteenth century, with the first home electric model introduced by Medela. Pumps let other caregivers feed babies and free mothers up. Nipple preference, sometimes called nipple confusion, is discussed as a bottle preference developed by some babies.

segments.title: Formula ingredients, water, and bottle warming
segments.summary: The hosts go through the FDA-required formula nutrient list, discuss fluoride supplements, the difference between organic and cheaper formulas, soy and coconut options for milk allergies, and the choice of ready-to-feed, concentrate, or powder. They cover using cold tap water, avoiding hot tap water due to lead, and warming bottles with a bottle warmer or water bath, testing on the forearm.

segments.title: Bottle sterilization, BPA, and safe feeding positions
segments.summary: The hosts discuss sterilizing new bottles and dishwashing, the 2012 US ban on BPA in baby bottles, the concern about BPS and BPF, and choosing opaque polyethylene or polypropylene bottles. They also cover glass bottles, skin-to-skin contact, holding babies upright, avoiding propped bottles, and the risks of ear infections, choking, tooth decay, and sleep association.

segments.title: Burping, feeding schedules, and fathers' involvement
segments.summary: The hosts explain alternating arms for eye development, keeping the nipple full to limit air, burping technique, scheduled versus demand feeding and tracking feeds, and encourage fathers to be involved in feeding and nighttime care regardless of feeding method.

segments.title: Listener suggestion: John Evans and American Interior
segments.summary: A listener suggests the story of Welsh explorer John Evans, who searched for a Welsh-speaking tribe in America, and the book, album, and film American Interior by David Evans of Super Furry Animals.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank the listener, give social media and email contact info, and sign off.
